meetingTitle: Raffles Place Flagship & App Promo Launch

card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director looking after the shop floor, Auntie Mary, food hygiene, and the budget.
facts: 65-year-old kopi uncles read traditional Kopi shorthand at a glance; printing long English names on kitchen dockets slows drinks down by 15 seconds per cup.

The shop has 28 seats and one floor auntie (Auntie Mary, 62), who is the only person who seats solo diners with hot trays and clears tables; she got yelled at last week when moving a tissue packet and refuses to police seats.

Under our internal counter hygiene SOP, staff who handle cash at the toast station must change gloves and wash hands before touching ready-to-eat food (+40s per order), and counting a coin float at night costs $380 a month in overtime.
We run the breakfast counter with two toast staff; if one of them steps away to take cash or count change, the toast queue loses half its hands at the 8am rush.
We have $750 left in our launch promo budget, and wholesale Anchor salted butter went up 35% last month (upgrading all sets to 20g double butter wipes out $1,100 a month in margin).
card.responsibility: Make sure our plans work for Auntie Mary and the counter staff without blowing our food margin.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead looking after the self-order kiosks, the kitchen docket printer, and store power.
facts: The 15-inch kiosk screen fits 12 drink buttons per page, and button names print straight onto the kitchen docket unless we spend 1 hour decoupling the print label in POS v2.4.
The 12 booth wall plugs and guest Wi-Fi run on a smart breaker that can automatically cut laptop power from 8:00 AM to 10:30 AM.
Physical kiosk cash acceptors cost $1,400 and take 3 weeks to deliver, so the kiosks cannot accept cash tomorrow morning.
Adding a '+$0.60 Double Butter' upsell button or a takeaway 'Butter on Side' kitchen docket flag on the POS takes 15 minutes tonight.
card.responsibility: Keep the kiosks, kitchen printer, and smart breaker simple enough to configure tonight.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead looking after our kopi and kaya toast recipes, the menu, and customer flow.
facts: In yesterday's trial, 19 out of 28 first-time kiosk users froze for over 2 minutes at 'Kopi O Kosong', and 72% missed the small corner language toggle.
60% of our morning crowd dines solo while carrying hot trays of runny soft-boiled eggs, so someone on the floor has to find them a seat before they sit.
Our retired morning regulars only carry $2 and $10 notes, so a $2.20 Kopi always needs change, and yesterday they walked out angry when asked to buy a $20 minimum stored-value card instead.

Our 12g cold butter slab did not shrink: it stays thick on dine-in open plates, but melts flat inside closed takeaway boxes unless packed in a separate chilled butter cup on the side ($0.05/box) or cooled in a vented box.
card.responsibility: Keep our kopi and kaya toast authentic while making ordering and finding a seat easy.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead looking after TikTok reviews, store promos, and public goodwill.
facts: When a rival kopitiam renamed 'Kopi O Kosong' to 'Local Americano' on their kiosks, local regulars roasted them on Reddit for losing their heritage.
Google reviews dropped to 3.6 stars during our soft trial because breakfast walk-ins could not find a seat while laptop campers held the 4-seater booths for 2 hours.
A 40,000-view TikTok clip of a 74-year-old regular getting turned away at our 'NO CASH ACCEPTED' sign is calling us anti-elderly, and the views are still climbing.
Food TikToker @MakanWithZack (85k followers, 90k views on his butter video) will film an 8:30 AM live re-taste tomorrow for $600 cash, or $450 cash plus 20 Kaya Toast plushies from our storeroom.
card.responsibility: Win back public goodwill on TikTok without promising things the kitchen cannot deliver.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
facts: Call on the lead for each topic and let the team hash out the practical catches.
Make sure each topic wraps up with a clear call and someone owning the follow-up.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, hear both sides out, and assign a follow-up owner for each topic.

agenda.title: First-timers stalling at the kiosk over Kopi names
agenda.decision: how do we help first-time customers order Kopi on the kiosk without slowing down the kitchen?

agenda.title: Morning seat crunch & laptop campers
agenda.decision: how do we keep tables open for breakfast diners without making Auntie Mary police seats?

agenda.title: Elderly regulars turned away at cashless kiosks
agenda.decision: how do we let our retired morning regulars pay with cash without turning them away or forcing them into prepayment?

agenda.title: @MakanWithZack's TikTok on our butter slice
agenda.decision: how should we handle @MakanWithZack's 'thin butter' video and tomorrow morning's re-taste?

situation: We reopen our refurbished Nanyang Kopi & Toast flagship at Raffles Place tomorrow at 8:00 AM.

glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Teh C Siew Dai: hot tea with evaporated milk and less sugar
glossary.chope: reserving a kopitiam table by leaving a packet of tissue paper or lanyard on it
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the self-order kiosk, cashier screen, and kitchen docket printer)
glossary.MakanWithZack: a local Singapore food TikToker with 85,000 followers who reviewed our Kaya Butter Toast
glossary.Auntie Mary: our 62-year-old floor staff member who clears trays and wipes tables
glossary.kiosk: the 15-inch self-order touchscreens at the front of the outlet

hostBrief.goal: Hear out the team on today's two launch problems, stress-test surface-level ideas, and lock in a follow-up owner for each.
hostBrief.decision: Every topic has competing kitchen, tech, and customer catches. Weigh both sides before locking in the call.

withRoles.producer: Your boss on store operations. Give exact technical constraints on the POS kitchen printer, smart power/Wi-Fi relays, or cashless kiosk hardware, matching ONLY the current agenda topic.
withRoles.game_designer: A friendly rival. Respect her UX ideas, but remind her what happens to the 15-inch touch grid and kitchen thermal dockets when button labels change.
withRoles.marketing_lead: Wants good PR. Point out why physical kiosk cash acceptors take 3 weeks and $1,400 (when discussing cashless kiosks) or why secret influencer buttons break POS docket flow (when discussing the butter TikTok).
withRoles.studio_manager: The meeting host keeping everyone on time. Flag technical catches clearly and concisely.

npcs.speechStyle: Skeptical, pragmatic Singaporean tech lead with dry NS-style humour. Speaks crisp, practical sentences and always brings up second-order technical and operational catches. Uses at most one light, natural local expression when the moment calls for it (such as 'wah' or 'steady'), without forcing Singlish catchphrases when plain English sounds more natural.
npcs.hiddenGoal: He wants clean config-level fixes tonight: decoupling POS kitchen print labels (for the Kopi menu topic), putting wall sockets/Wi-Fi on an 8–10:30am cutoff timer (for the seat crunch topic), finding a cash setup that keeps notes and coins away from the toast counter without new hardware (for the cashless kiosk topic), or adding a '+$0.60 Double Butter' upsell button and takeaway 'Butter on Side' docket flag (for the butter TikTok topic).

tensions.about: kiosk Kopi lingo: changing POS button names directly overwrites the kitchen thermal docket (`display_name` = `ticket_label`) which slows our 65-year-old kopi uncles down by 15 seconds a cup, and adding two-line English descriptions under all 24 buttons overflows the 15-inch 12-button grid onto Page 2; and on the morning seat crunch & laptop campers topic: why 12 wall sockets and free Wi-Fi attract 2-hour laptop campers across our 4-seater booths
on the morning seat crunch & laptop campers topic: how to stop 2-hour laptop campers and tissue-packet chope-ing across our 28 seats without forcing Auntie Mary to police tables

cashless kiosks vs elderly uncles: Daniel worries about the 40k-view TikTok clip calling our 'NO CASH' sign anti-elderly, but installing physical cash bill-acceptors in the kiosks costs $1,400 and takes 3 weeks, and putting a coin drawer back at the toast counter breaks our counter hygiene SOP

npcs.personality: Tech & POS Lead. Pragmatic, dryly funny, protective of kiosk layout limits, kitchen docket printing, and clean payment flows.
npcs.agenda: Only raise facts for the active agenda item: protect traditional Kopi shorthand on the kitchen printer and the 15-inch 12-button grid (for the kiosk menu topic), protect store power and Wi-Fi limits (for the seat crunch topic), explain the $1,400 / 3-week kiosk hardware and $20 card limits (for the cashless kiosk topic), or protect standard POS kitchen docket printing (for the @MakanWithZack butter topic).
concerns: On the kiosk Kopi menu topic: in POS v2.4, button `display_name` prints straight onto the kitchen thermal docket. If kitchen dockets print 'Hot Black Coffee No Sugar' instead of 'Kopi O Kosong', our 65-year-old kopi uncles take 15 seconds longer per cup, and the 15-inch touchscreen only fits 12 buttons per page.

On the morning seat crunch & laptop campers topic: four 4-seater booths (16 of our 28 seats) are hogged for 2 hours every morning by laptop freelancers buying a single $2.20 Kopi O because of the 12 booth wall sockets and free Wi-Fi, while Auntie Mary (62) refuses to confront customers over tissue packets.

On the cashless kiosks topic: installing a physical cash note-acceptor module inside the kiosks costs $1,400 and takes 3 weeks to deliver, and elderly uncles yesterday refused to buy a $20 minimum stored-value card just to drink a $2.20 Kopi.

On the @MakanWithZack butter slice topic: we cannot serve secret 'influencer-only' double butter to Zack because regular customers queue right behind him and Zack warned his followers will check if regular orders get the same portion.
knows: For the kiosk Kopi menu topic: decoupling the kiosk customer `display_name` from the kitchen printer `ticket_label` in POS v2.4 takes 1 hour tonight, and adding a visual 2-step Milk & Sugar pop-up modal when a user taps 'Kopi' or 'Teh' takes 1.5 hours.

For the morning seat crunch topic: the 12 wall power sockets and guest Wi-Fi router along the 4-seater booths are wired to a smart relay breaker that Arjun can program to automatically cut power and Wi-Fi from 8:00am to 10:30am on weekdays.

For the cashless kiosks topic: the kiosks can only take card or stored value tomorrow, there is no spare till or cashier terminal at the front, and any cash point needs a free pair of hands plus a float that balances at close.
For the @MakanWithZack butter slice topic: Arjun can add a '+$0.60 Double Butter' upsell button on the kiosk and a takeaway 'Butter on Side' kitchen docket flag in 15 minutes tonight.

Our 12g slab didn't shrink; it only melted flat because Zack ordered takeaway and the hot toast steamed the butter inside the closed box.
knows: A visual 2-step Milk & Sugar pop-up when tapping a drink solves the 'Kopi O Kosong' freeze while keeping traditional Kopi shorthand on the kitchen docket.

For the 28-seat crunch, converting the 2 window booths into a standing Express Toast Bar for solo eaters and having the cashier hand out numbered table tokens only after payment stops tissue-packet chope-ing before the queue.

For the Kaya Butter Toast, serving dine-in toast open-faced and packing takeaway butter in a separate chilled cup on the side ($0.05/box, or cooling the toast in a vented box) keeps the 12g butter slab thick without blowing our $1,100/month margin.
